mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which signals economic strength and drives up S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% and SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains above 4.5% and SPX 60-day returns are positive more than 50% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both show strong growth, it indicates increased demand, boosting corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both HOUST and RSAFS grow by over 5% YoY and SPX 20-day returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) during an economic expansion signals increased supply and productivity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO grows by over 3% YoY and SPX 60-day returns are negative more than 30% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased consumer and business spending, thus driving up S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is below 2% and SPX 5-day returns are negative more than 40% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth exceeds 200k and SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 35% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) both indicate strong economic growth, it signals high demand, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 and HOUST both grow by over 4% YoY and SPX 60-day returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle indicates lower borrowing costs, stimulating investment and increasing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases by 25bps and SPX 20-day returns are negative more than 45% of the time, the hypothesis is rejected.
